AggregationMethod.description:
How a timeseries should be aggregated by default, e.g. in coarser intervals

AVG is an alias of MEAN.
AggregationMethod.title: AggregationMethod

InheritedMetricMetadata.description:
Properties a metric inherits from objects higher up in a hierarchy

Arbitrary fields, e.g. the latitude of the plant a sensor belongs to. Typically the deepest
occurrence in the hierarchy wins. Should not contain the fields the conventions define for
metrics and value dimensions, like "name", "id" or "unit": Consumers only use inherited
properties as last resort and not for information describing the metric itself, like its
unit or names.

The values should have the JSON type matching their meaning: numbers as numbers, booleans as
booleans and points in time as UTC isoformat strings, not e.g. a number as string.

E.g. the hetida platform provides the effective property values of a signal here, keyed by
property label: its own values, otherwise the value of the nearest asset above it having one.
InheritedMetricMetadata.title: InheritedMetricMetadata

IntervalType.description:
Which boundaries belong to a time interval

closed: both, open: none, left_closed / right_open: only the start,
right_closed / left_open: only the end.
IntervalType.title: IntervalType

MetricComment.description:
A comment attached to a metric, describing a time range of its timeseries data

E.g. the hetida platform provides the comments on a signal whose time range overlaps the
queried interval and which existed at query time, newest first.

Start and end of the time range must be provided together. They are equal for a comment on a
single point in time.

edited_at.description: When the comment was last edited. Null or missing if never edited.
edited_at.title: Edited At

end_date.description: End of the time range the comment refers to
end_date.title: End Date

id.description: Id of the comment, e.g. a UUID
id.title: Id

replies.description: Replies to the comment, oldest first
replies.title: Replies

start_date.description: Start of the time range the comment refers to
start_date.title: Start Date

tags.description: Free text tags classifying the comment
tags.title: Tags

username.description: Username of the author of the comment
username.title: Username

MetricComment.title: MetricComment

MetricCommentReply.description: A reply to a comment attached to a metric

edited_at.description: When the reply was last edited. Null or missing if never edited.
edited_at.title: Edited At

id.description: Id of the reply, e.g. a UUID
id.title: Id

username.description: Username of the author of the reply
username.title: Username

MetricCommentReply.title: MetricCommentReply

MetricMetadata.description:
Metadata of a metric, i.e. of a single, possibly multidimensional timeseries

A metric is identified by its field named by dataset_metadata.metric_key, whose values occur
in the metric column of a MULTITSFRAME. Every metric must have this field as a string,
unique among the metrics.

channel_id.description: Actual platform channel id. Deprecated, since the platform calls channels signals now.
channel_id.title: Channel Id

comments.description: Comments attached to the metric, describing situations in its timeseries data
comments.title: Comments

data_frequency.description: Interval in which values of the metric are recorded as Pandas date offset alias or timedelta string, e.g. "15min" or "1D": For recording_mode periodic the interval between subsequent values, for on_change the interval after which the value is recorded again at the latest, also without a change (heartbeat). Together with data_frequency_offset and data_frequency_timezone it takes precedence over ref_data_frequency, ref_data_frequency_offset and ref_data_frequency_timezone of the dataset metadata for this metric.
data_frequency.title: Data Frequency

data_frequency_offset.description: Offset of the timestamps against the starts of the intervals of data_frequency (see data_frequency_timezone) as timedelta string, e.g. "4min": not negative and smaller than data_frequency. 0 if missing or null. Requires data_frequency.
data_frequency_offset.title: Data Frequency Offset

data_frequency_timezone.description: Time zone the intervals of data_frequency are aligned to, as IANA time zone name like "Europe/Berlin" or "UTC" (preferred, since it respects daylight saving time) or as fixed UTC offset like "+02:00". Without it, the intervals start at the multiples of data_frequency since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. With it, for a data_frequency shorter than a day, the intervals restart at each local midnight: They start at local midnight plus multiples of data_frequency, and the last interval of a day ends at the next local midnight, so it may be shorter, e.g. on the day of a daylight saving time change. For a data_frequency of a day or longer, the intervals follow the calendar of the time zone, e.g. days from local midnight to local midnight. The offset shifts the intervals in both cases. Requires data_frequency.
data_frequency_timezone.title: Data Frequency Timezone

default_aggregation_method.description: How the timeseries should be aggregated by default, e.g. when components plot or report it in coarser intervals. If missing or null: LAST if the value_data_type of the value dimension "value" is boolean or string, otherwise MEAN. AVG is an alias of MEAN. E.g. the hetida platform provides the method it aggregates the signal with when bucketing it, for a signal group member the one configured for the member.

default_timezone.description: Time zone the timeseries should be evaluated in by default, as IANA time zone name like "Europe/Berlin" or "UTC" (preferred, since it respects daylight saving time) or as fixed UTC offset like "+02:00". Components evaluating the timeseries in calendar intervals use it, e.g. a report aggregating days, which start at midnight of this time zone, so the results differ between time zones. This is not the time zone timestamps are displayed in: That is the plot target timezone of the execution context, which depends on the viewer, while this time zone belongs to the data, e.g. the time zone of the plant. Falls back to dataset_metadata.default_timezone.
default_timezone.title: Default Timezone

display_name.description: A shorter name for labels, captions or plot titles
display_name.title: Display Name

external_id.description: Unique id / key in external source systems. Often used to identify the metric in the metric column, i.e. as metric_key.
external_id.title: External Id

id.description: Id of the metric, also if another field identifies the metric in the data via dataset_metadata.metric_key. E.g. the hetida platform provides the signal id here.
id.title: Id

origin.description: Where the values come from, as free text of the source system, e.g. "OPC_UA", "MQTT" or "FORM" for values entered manually.
origin.title: Origin

path.description: Location of the metric in the hierarchy of its source system: the names of the levels from the top down to the object the metric belongs to, without the metric itself, e.g. ["Plant A", "Pickling Unit", "Influx"]. Corresponds to the breadcrumb path of the sources of generic REST adapters.
path.title: Path

recording_aggregation_method.description: Only for recording_mode periodic: how each value aggregates the values of the interval [timestamp, timestamp + data_frequency), e.g. MEAN for an average or MAX for a maximum. Null or missing if the values are samples, e.g. the value holding at the timestamp.

recording_mode.description: When the values are recorded. Unknown if missing or null. periodic requires data_frequency (or dataset_metadata.ref_data_frequency).

short_display_name.description: A short name for legends in plots
short_display_name.title: Short Display Name

value_dimensions.description: Metadata of the value dimensions of this metric: an entry for each value column of the data, i.e. exactly the value dimension "value" for a SERIES. Each column may occur at most once.
value_dimensions.title: Value Dimensions

MetricMetadata.title: MetricMetadata

MultiTSFrameDatasetMetadata.description:
Metadata associated with a MULTITSFRAME as a whole

E.g. the queried time interval or how existing data should be handled when the dataset is
sent to an adapter. The fields concerning invalidation and deletion are only relevant for
adapters actually supporting these operations, like the built-in SQL adapter. Other adapters
may ignore them.

Start and end of an interval must be provided together.

default_aggregation_interval.description: Interval to aggregate the timeseries to by default, e.g. when components plot or report them, as Pandas date offset alias or timedelta string, e.g. "15min" or "1D". The metrics are aggregated with their default_aggregation_method. E.g. a hetida platform signal group is configured with such an interval.
default_aggregation_interval.title: Default Aggregation Interval

default_timezone.description: Time zone the timeseries should be evaluated in by default, as IANA time zone name like "Europe/Berlin" or "UTC" (preferred, since it respects daylight saving time) or as fixed UTC offset like "+02:00". Components evaluating the timeseries in calendar intervals use it, e.g. a report aggregating days, which start at midnight of this time zone, so the results differ between time zones. This is not the time zone timestamps are displayed in: That is the plot target timezone of the execution context, which depends on the viewer, while this time zone belongs to the data, e.g. the time zone of the plant. Applies to all metrics without their own default_timezone.
default_timezone.title: Default Timezone

delete_invalidated.description: Whether data to be invalidated should be deleted instead. What null means is up to the adapter. Adapters do not need to support deletion.
delete_invalidated.title: Delete Invalidated

invalidate_dataset.description: Whether existing data should be invalidated: in the invalidation interval if specified, otherwise in the ref interval. If neither is specified, a closed ref interval from the first to the last datapoint is inferred. Without datapoints no invalidation can occur then. What null means is up to the adapter.
invalidate_dataset.title: Invalidate Dataset

invalidation_interval_end.description: End of an invalidation interval separate from the ref interval in UTC isoformat
invalidation_interval_end.title: Invalidation Interval End

invalidation_interval_start.description: Start of an invalidation interval separate from the ref interval in UTC isoformat
invalidation_interval_start.title: Invalidation Interval Start

invalidation_timestamp.description: Invalidation timestamp for all invalidated datapoints. If null, the execution_timestamp query parameter sent to generic REST adapters or, if that is not present either, the current time should be used.
invalidation_timestamp.title: Invalidation Timestamp

metric_key.description: Which field of the metric objects under metrics identifies a metric, i.e. occurs in the metric column of a MULTITSFRAME, e.g. "id" or "external_id".
metric_key.title: Metric Key

new_data_invalidation_date.description: An invalidation date to be stored together with all new datapoints, i.e. invalidating them in advance. Ignored if null.
new_data_invalidation_date.title: New Data Invalidation Date

only_invalidate.description: If true, existing data should only be invalidated and the new data should not be stored. Cannot be true if invalidate_dataset is false.
only_invalidate.title: Only Invalidate

queried_metrics.description: The requested metrics. Since not all queried metrics may have data in the queried interval, a metric may be missing in the data.
queried_metrics.title: Queried Metrics

query_timestamp.description: The point in time whose state of the data was delivered in UTC isoformat: Data stored, changed or invalidated later is not included. A source supporting it delivers the same data again when queried for this point in time, e.g. for reproducing an execution.
query_timestamp.title: Query Timestamp

ref_data_frequency.description: Frequency of the timeseries as Pandas date offset alias or timedelta string, e.g. "15min" or "1D": the data_frequency of all metrics without their own, with the same meaning as there. Together with ref_data_frequency_offset and ref_data_frequency_timezone.
ref_data_frequency.title: Ref Data Frequency

ref_data_frequency_offset.description: Offset of the timestamps against the starts of the intervals of ref_data_frequency (see ref_data_frequency_timezone) as timedelta string, e.g. "4min": not negative and smaller than ref_data_frequency. 0 if missing or null. Requires ref_data_frequency. Applies to all metrics without their own data_frequency.
ref_data_frequency_offset.title: Ref Data Frequency Offset

ref_data_frequency_timezone.description: Time zone the intervals of ref_data_frequency are aligned to, as IANA time zone name like "Europe/Berlin" or "UTC" (preferred, since it respects daylight saving time) or as fixed UTC offset like "+02:00". Without it, the intervals start at the multiples of ref_data_frequency since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. With it, for a ref_data_frequency shorter than a day, the intervals restart at each local midnight: They start at local midnight plus multiples of ref_data_frequency, and the last interval of a day ends at the next local midnight, so it may be shorter, e.g. on the day of a daylight saving time change. For a ref_data_frequency of a day or longer, the intervals follow the calendar of the time zone, e.g. days from local midnight to local midnight. The offset shifts the intervals in both cases. Requires ref_data_frequency. Applies to all metrics without their own data_frequency.
ref_data_frequency_timezone.title: Ref Data Frequency Timezone

ref_dataset_discrete.description: Whether the ref dataset should be considered as discrete, i.e. isolated datapoints instead of an interval. If true, the ref interval is not required.
ref_dataset_discrete.title: Ref Dataset Discrete

ref_interval_end_timestamp.description: End of the queried time interval (ref interval) in UTC isoformat. Required unless ref_dataset_discrete is true.
ref_interval_end_timestamp.title: Ref Interval End Timestamp

ref_interval_start_timestamp.description: Start of the queried time interval (ref interval) in UTC isoformat. Required unless ref_dataset_discrete is true.
ref_interval_start_timestamp.title: Ref Interval Start Timestamp

ref_interval_type.description: Type of the ref interval. Required unless ref_dataset_discrete is true.

single_metric.description: If the MULTITSFRAME holds a single metric: its metric_key field value. Must not be set if more than one metric is present.
single_metric.title: Single Metric

MultiTSFrameDatasetMetadata.title: MultiTSFrameDatasetMetadata

MultiTSFrameMetadata.description:
hetida designer metadata conventions for a MULTITSFRAME

Structure of the metadata in the attrs attribute of a MULTITSFRAME during execution, which
is also exchanged with adapters, e.g. via the Data-Attributes header of the generic REST
adapter multitsframe endpoint or via the __metadata__ field of the wrapped format of the
direct provisioning adapter.

The fields that are not required are optional. Additional fields are allowed at every level.
Timestamps are UTC isoformat strings with explicit offset (Z or +00:00).

metrics.description: Metadata of the metrics: one for each metric in the data. Each metric must have the field named by dataset_metadata.metric_key as a string, unique among the metrics.
metrics.title: Metrics

value_dimensions_shared.description: Metadata of value dimensions that have the same meaning for all metrics. Consumers use it as fallback, but it does not replace the value dimensions of the metrics. Each column may occur at most once.
value_dimensions_shared.title: Value Dimensions Shared

MultiTSFrameMetadata.title: MultiTSFrameMetadata

RecordingMode.description:
When the values of a timeseries are recorded

periodic: one value per interval of data_frequency, timestamped with the start of the
interval. A missing value is a gap.
on_change: a value is recorded when it changes (by more than the deadband of its value
dimension) and holds until the next one. Missing timestamps are no gaps, as long as
data_frequency (the heartbeat) is not exceeded.
irregular: values at arbitrary points in time.
RecordingMode.title: RecordingMode

SeriesMetadata.description:
hetida designer metadata conventions for a SERIES

Structure of the metadata in the attrs attribute of a SERIES during execution, which is also
exchanged with adapters, e.g. via the Data-Attributes header of the generic REST adapter
timeseries endpoint (for each timeseries) or via the __metadata__ field of the wrapped format
of the direct provisioning adapter.

The fields that are not required are optional. Additional fields are allowed at every level.
Timestamps are UTC isoformat strings with explicit offset (Z or +00:00).

metrics.description: Metadata of the single metric: exactly one metric, which has the field named by dataset_metadata.metric_key with the value of dataset_metadata.single_metric.
metrics.title: Metrics

value_dimensions_shared.description: Metadata of value dimensions that have the same meaning for all metrics. Consumers use it as fallback, but it does not replace the value dimensions of the metrics. Each column may occur at most once.
value_dimensions_shared.title: Value Dimensions Shared

SeriesMetadata.title: SeriesMetadata

SharedValueDimensionMetadata.description:
Metadata of a value dimension shared by all metrics

Every column of a MULTITSFRAME besides "timestamp" and "metric" and every column of a
SINGLETSFRAME besides "timestamp" defines a value dimension for each metric. A SERIES has
exactly one value dimension, which is "value".

column.description: The actual column name in the MULTITSFRAME or SINGLETSFRAME, connecting the value dimension to its column. "value" for a SERIES.
column.title: Column

deadband.description: For a metric with recording_mode on_change: the change of the values, in their unit, which has to be exceeded for a value to be recorded. 0 records every change.
deadband.title: Deadband

decimals.description: Number of decimal places numeric values should be displayed with, in their unit, e.g. 2 for 12.35. Only affects how values are displayed, e.g. in tables, tooltips or reports; the values themselves are not rounded. Up to the consumer if missing or null.
decimals.title: Decimals

description.description: A description. Should be considered empty if missing.
description.title: Description

display_name.description: A shorter name for labels, captions or plot titles. Falls back to name.
display_name.title: Display Name

name.description: Name of the value dimension, e.g. "temperature". May equal column.
name.title: Name

short_display_name.description: A short name for legends in plots. Falls back to display_name.
short_display_name.title: Short Display Name

unit.description: Unit of the values, e.g. "°C" or "m/s", "" for dimensionless quantities
unit.title: Unit

SharedValueDimensionMetadata.title: SharedValueDimensionMetadata

SignalGroupMetadata.description:
A group of signals a dataset was read from

E.g. the hetida platform provides the signal group a MULTITSFRAME was read from.
SignalGroupMetadata.title: SignalGroupMetadata
